January 27, 1956
Due to my extensive wanderings, the November '55 issue of The Diamond has just caught
up with me, and now perhaps, feeling firmly planted in Syracuse, I can raise my voice in
behalf of Psi Upsilon.
It was very heartwarming to read about such a worthy project as the Psi Upsilon Scholarship
Fund which has been initiated by the Psi and Upsilon Alumni. As stated in the article, the
Fund will provide financial assistance for certain undergraduates who might otherwise have
to forego the fellowship of fraternity life or full
participation in other college activities. I
enthusiastically endorse this plan, for I can recall vividly the similar problems encountered as
a freshman at the Delta.

The aims and accomplishments of a fraternity, which we as alumni so well know, are stated
in part in the article as follows :
"He derives a sense of stewardship which makes him a better citizen and a technique for
'getting along,' which improves his chances to contribute to society."
The daily problems we are confronted with would, indeed, be easier to handle if we only
knew how to 'get along' with our fellow man. Fraternity life does help mold the immature
freshman into the mature graduate who will practice good citizenship and good fellowship.
Brothers Nicholas E. Brown, Upsilon '28, Wilard B. Eddy, Psi '14, and Walter V. Wiard,
Upsilon '22, are to be heartily congratulated for inaugurating so worthy a
project, I hope, that
will be endorsed by all Psi U's and become a project of the Psi Upsilon Fraternity.
Yours in the bonds,
John S. Skillman, Delta '46
